paragraphs.text: Made of malice, in which is steeped the venom of all vices.
paragraphs.anchor: Deliver me O Lord, from the evil man

paragraphs.text: Man of violences, who, vulture-like, {Rev 11:10} liveth by rapine. Such were Saul and his informers.
paragraphs.anchor: Preserve me from the violent man

paragraphs.text: Where the devil worketh night and day as a mintman; as a smith in his forge; or an artificer in his shop. A godly man is said to have right thoughts, Pro 12:5, and that his desires are only good, Pro 11:23. An evil man is called a man of wicked devices, Pro 12:2; Pro 14:17, being ingeniose nequam, wittily wicked, as it was once said of Gaius Curio, the Roman lawyer.
paragraphs.anchor: Which imagine mischief in their heart

paragraphs.text: Heb. they gather wars, as serpents gather poison to vomit out at others. Coacervant praelia, q.d. sunt tanquam tubae belli.
paragraphs.anchor: They are gathered together for war

paragraphs.text: Which, by reason of his sharp tongue, striketh more deeply.
paragraphs.anchor: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent

paragraphs.text: Adders’poison] Venenum Ptyados. R. Solomen readeth spiders’ poison; others, asps!, vipers’; malice turneth men into serpents, saith Chrysostom.
Who am thus sought and set for; but thou canst rescue me.
Praecipitare, to hurl me down headlong.
They are restless to ruin me, adding all kind of craft to their cruelty.

paragraphs.text: Danger drove David home to God; as bugbears do little children to their parents.
Heb. of armours; for battle David never had any with Saul, but declined it.
For if they should be votorum compotes, masters of their desires, they would be intolerably insolent, so as to say, Our high hand, and not the Lord, hath done all this, Deu 32:27.

The chieftain, the ringleader, Doeg, or Saul himself. Or thus, let mischief cover the heads of my besiegers, let it fall upon their pates, as Psa 7:16 Similitudo est a sacrificiis, quorum capita execrabantur.
Conflagrent ut corruant. Haec sunt non tam vota quam vaticinia.
paragraphs.anchor: Let burning coals fall upon them

paragraphs.text: Heb. a man of tongue, whereof Geraldus reckoneth up twenty-four several sins; a world of wickedness, St James calleth it, Jas 3:6

The angel of death shall hunt him into hell, saith the Chaldee. Of the blackbird’s excrements is made bird lime, to catch him. Gaius Marius was slain with the sword he made when he was a cutler. Propiis pennis perire grave est, was Julian’s motto. God’s judgments against sinners are feathered from themselves, as a fowl shot with an arrow feathered from her own body.
paragraphs.anchor: Evil shall hunt the violent man
